svg.title: Prefill and decode, step by step
svg.desc: Prefill and decode, step by step, for one layer's query table in Llama 3 8B, whose dimension is 4,096. Top, prefill: the whole prompt of 1,000 tokens is a table of 1,000 by 4,096, multiplied by the 4,096 by 4,096 query weights to give a result of 1,000 by 4,096, cut into tiles. All compute cores are lit. Each tile of weights crosses the link once and is then used 1,000 times on the chip, and every group of cores works at the same time. It is compute-bound: the cores never wait; about 16 trillion calculations, at least 16 milliseconds, the time to first token. Bottom, decode: one new token is a single row, 1 by 4,096, times the same 4,096 by 4,096 weights, giving a single row. The cores are only dimly lit. Every tile still crosses the link, all 16 GB, used for just 1 token; each core gets a sliver of work, 1 row instead of 1,000. It is memory-bound: the cores mostly wait, about 0.02 milliseconds of maths against about 5 milliseconds of reading, at most about 200 tokens a second.
svg.text: Prefill and decode, step by step
One layer's query table in Llama 3 8B. Each token is a vector of 4,096 numbers: the model's dimension.
PREFILL · THE WHOLE PROMPT AT ONCE
Each tile of weights crosses the link once,
then is used 1,000 times on the chip.
Every group of cores works at the same time,
DECODE · ONE TOKEN AT A TIME
Every tile still crosses the link, all 16 GB,
to be used for just 1 token.
The work is shared out, but each core
≈ 0.02 ms of maths vs ≈ 5 ms of reading:
